text:
sara: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking about simplifying the ephemeral credential surface for S2S. Problem: we have too many token variants (project-scoped, route-scoped, long-lived API keys, delegated proxies). Proposal idea: one canonical short-lived machine token + optional attestation envelope for extra scoping. Goal: reduce runtime branching and token-issuing complexity.

leo: +1 to fewer variants. My main worry: long-running batch/cron jobs that can't re-request tokens frequently. How do we support TTL vs renewals without opening long-lived keys?

ajohnson: We can allow a short-lived refresh handle for hosts (not apps) — exchangeable only from a pinned IP/VPC and audited. Prefer avoiding permanent keys in code.

maria: Operational note: issuer load will spike if every route asks for fresh tokens. Suggest a caching tier (5m) and prefixing by actor+route signature to reuse tokens safely.

leo: Right — tradeoff: reuse reduces issuance QPS but slightly widens blast radius. Documented TTL windows needed.

infra-bot: ephemeral-token-issuer v2 deployed to staging :rocket: (metrics behind /infra/ephemeral/issuer)

ajohnson: Key UX question — per-route claims vs per-service token. Per-route = least privilege but multiplies tokens and routing logic. Per-service = simpler but coarser permissions. Thoughts?

sara: For initial rollout I'd favor per-service token with optional attestation envelope containing route-bound claims. Gateway can enforce envelope if present; fallback to service token otherwise. That lets us incrementally tighten.

maria: Implementation detail: attestation envelope can be a signed JSON blob with `origin`, `route`, `nonce`, `exp` fields. We should include `audit_id` in the envelope so logs correlate to issuance. Example header: `Authorization: Bearer svc:ephemeral/<svc-id>\nX-Attestation: eyJhbGci...`

sec-lead: Important: maintain backward compat with API keys for customer workloads. Plan a 3-month grace where API keys are mapped to read-only ephemeral proxies, and require migration tooling. Also require audit hooks in issuer to emit policy decisions to SIEM.

leo: Also need deterministic fallback semantics in the runtime: if envelope validation fails, either 401 or allow with reduced privileges — decide per route.

ajohnson: I can prototype a sidecar pattern (issuer running next to service) vs centralized gateway exchange to compare latencies. Will instrument 95/99p latencies.

sara: Nice. Next steps: small spike for sidecar prototype + gateway exchange, write integration tests for cron job renewal, and draft migration plan for API keys. I'll open a follow-up RFC PR with implementation sketch. Please add comments on the PR.

maria: quick ops ask — include a control-plane knob to throttle issuance per-service to protect the issuer during rollouts.

sec-lead: Security checklist we need on RFC: threat model for token leakage, rotation/rotation-orphan handling, audit schema, and secrets lifecycle (KMS/HSM integration).

sara: Created RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/921 — please review by EOD Friday :eyes:

leo: Reviewing now. :thumbsup:

ajohnson: I'll pair with infra on the spike Mon/Tue.

infra-bot: Added spike task to #infra-board: https://taskboard.internal/boards/3721 (assignee: ajohnson)

sara: thanks everyone — will sync in tomorrow standup if there are blockers.
